program.improvement: Harness-level: plugin/skill/hook/MCP actually load and run; confirmation predicates fail closed on missing artifacts; test runners execute FAIL_TO_PASS; not a weight-level capability bump.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench
benchmarks.measures: Whether an agent can edit a real GitHub repository so that FAIL_TO_PASS tests start passing and PASS_TO_PASS tests stay green.
benchmarks.does_not_measure: Raw next-token coding skill on a docstring (HumanEval) or knowledge QA; also does not isolate harness quality from retrieval quality unless the retriever is ablated.
benchmarks.contamination_status: UNMEASURED as a detector with a false-positive rate. Authors' Table 7 date split is not a contamination test: Claude 2 oracle 4.87% before 2023 vs 4.23% after 2023.
benchmarks.saturation_status: Not saturated in the introducing paper (best BM25 Claude 2 1.96%). Later public forks (Verified/Pro) are a different row.
benchmarks.strongest_caveat: The 4.80% oracle figure (Table 18) uses gold-edited files; it is an upper bound on retrieval, not a claim that the harness is solved. GPT-4 oracle is a 25% subset.

benchmarks.name: τ-bench
benchmarks.measures: Whether a tool-using agent can finish a user conversation so the database matches the annotated goal AND it follows domain policy, measured as pass^1 and reliability pass^k.
benchmarks.does_not_measure: Repo patch quality, GUI grounding, or knowledge QA. User utterances are LM-simulated.
benchmarks.contamination_status: Synthetic schema/API/tasks; not a public GitHub-issue dump. Contamination rate UNMEASURED (no canary study in the paper).
benchmarks.saturation_status: Not saturated in the paper: gpt-4o function-calling 61.2% retail / 35.2% airline; pass^8 < 25% retail.
benchmarks.strongest_caveat: pass^k uses LM-sampled user and agent turns; temperature 0.0 agent / 1.0 user. A harness that only lifts pass^1 can still be unreliable at pass^8.

benchmarks.name: AgentBench
benchmarks.measures: LLM-as-agent success across eight interactive environments; the OS/DB slices measure shell and structured-tool interaction.
benchmarks.does_not_measure: This program's confirmation predicate, plugin marketplace install, or GUI desktop use. Game/puzzle slices (DCG, LTP) are not harness-plugin tests.
benchmarks.contamination_status: UNMEASURED. Environments are interactive simulators, not a static leaked test set, but no canary/FP study is reported.
benchmarks.saturation_status: Not saturated in Table 3: gpt-4 overall 4.01 vs llama-2-70b 0.78; OS 42.4 vs 9.7.
benchmarks.strongest_caveat: OA is a weighted average (Section 4.1), not a raw capability. Only the OS/DB slices are claimed as detectors for this program's hook/shell surface.

benchmarks.name: HumanEval
benchmarks.measures: Functional correctness of a Python function synthesized from a docstring, via pass@k unit tests.
benchmarks.does_not_measure: Multi-file repo repair, tool/MCP invocation, plugin loading, hooks, or confirmation predicates.
benchmarks.contamination_status: Subsequent literature treats HumanEval as contaminated for later models; the introducing paper does not report a contamination detector FP rate (UNMEASURED).
benchmarks.saturation_status: Saturated as a frontier agent metric: it is a 164-problem function-completion set, not an agent harness eval.
benchmarks.strongest_caveat: A popular coding number that is routinely cited as 'agent' performance. It is not. Codex-12B 28.81% pass@1 vs GPT-3 ~0% is a pretraining/finetune effect.

benchmarks.name: MMLU

benchmarks.does_not_measure: Tool use, repo editing, plugin loading, hooks, MCP, or any harness loop.
benchmarks.contamination_status: Later work documents train-set leakage for many MMLU items; the introducing paper does not give a detector FP rate (UNMEASURED).

benchmarks.name: OSWorld

benchmarks.does_not_measure: Plugin/hook/MCP loading in a CLI coding harness, confirmation predicates, or SWE-style patch tests.

benchmarks.saturation_status: Not saturated vs humans in the paper: GPT-4 a11y-tree 12.24% vs human 72.36%. Still inapplicable to THIS program.

benchmarks.name: WebArena
benchmarks.measures: End-to-end success rate of a web agent following natural-language commands on realistic self-hosted sites.
benchmarks.does_not_measure: This program's plugin/hook/MCP/confirmation surface. No WebArena browser environment ships here.
benchmarks.contamination_status: Self-hosted sites reduce copy-paste of live web answers; no canary FP rate (UNMEASURED).
benchmarks.saturation_status: Not saturated in the paper: best GPT-4 14.41% vs human 78.24% (Table 2). Still inapplicable to THIS program.
benchmarks.strongest_caveat: Table 2's 14.41% is GPT-4 CoT without the unachievable-task hint; the CoT+UA-hint GPT-4 cell is 11.70%. Citing 14.41% without the human 78.24% would be E3.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified (public set)
benchmarks.measures: Intended: a 500-problem human-filtered subset of SWE-bench with fairer tests. In 2026 OpenAI stopped using it as a frontier signal.
benchmarks.does_not_measure: Clean harness-level improvement on the public set: remaining failures mix broken tests and memorized gold patches.
benchmarks.contamination_status: OpenAI 2026 blog: frontier models reproduced gold patches verbatim on some tasks. No numeric contamination rate is given (that claim is E3). Broken-test prevalence on the o3-fail audit is E2.
benchmarks.saturation_status: OpenAI treats the public Verified set as no longer a frontier coding signal (Feb 2026 blog).
benchmarks.strongest_caveat: The 59.4% figure is of 138 o3-fail problems (27.6% of 500), not of the whole set. It cannot be restated as '59.4% of SWE-bench Verified is broken'.
